## Appearance

Isolde is an attractive young woman with dark hair, dark eyes, rosy cheeks, and charming dimples inherited from her mother. She has a plumper, curvier figure than Nell, which she occasionally frets over in her youth, and eventually matures into a matronly figure. She possesses an excellent taste in dress, frequently wearing stylish outfits such as wild-rose pink gowns, fur caps, and a ring on her left hand after her engagement.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P40](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0040), [v1 c19 P35](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0035), [v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002), [v3 c33 P9](../source/v03-c33.md#nw-v03-c33-p0009), [v4 c1 P2](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0002)_

## Personality

Isolde is cheerful, pragmatic, and affectionate, possessing a lighthearted humor and a tendency to laugh easily. Though grounded in practical matters and occasionally skeptical of imaginative or romantic extremes, she is fiercely loyal to her bosom friend, Nell Harcourt, and participates enthusiastically in their shared adventures. She values neatness and propriety, showing a strong sense of duty to her home, family, and religious community.

_Sources: [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P26](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0026), [v1 c12 P30](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0030), [v1 c12 P37](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0037), [v1 c15 P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 c15 P6](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0006), [v1 c17 P5](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0005)_

## History

Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill near Brierley. At eleven years old, she became the bosom friend and confidante of Nell Harcourt, sealing their friendship with a solemn 'oath' over an imaginary stream in her garden. Together they created playhouses such as Larkrise, named local spots, and attended Brierley school together, where Isolde excelled academically and socially. Despite initial friction when her mother briefly forbade her from playing with Nell over a currant wine misunderstanding, Isolde remained devoted to her friend.

Throughout her teenage years, Isolde shared in Nell's school adventures, social gatherings, and the Brierley Village Improvement Society. In her late teens, she fell in love with Gideon Duckett, eventually becoming engaged to him. Following Nell's graduation from Regent's Academy, Isolde married Gideon at Pear Hill. She settled down near Brierley as a homemaker, eventually becoming the mother of children including Small Nell Lucinda and young Gideon, remaining Nell's closest confidante through all of life's changes.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c12 P25](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0025), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c15 P3](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0003), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c17 P3](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0003), [v1 c29 P11](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0011), [v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002), [v3 c29 P15](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0015), [v4 c1 P2](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0002)_

- Daughter of Mrs. Pembroke and Mr. Pembroke of Pear Hill  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c12 P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014)</sub>
- Grew up near Grey Shutters with younger sisters  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c12 P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027)</sub>
- Great-niece of Miss Lavinia Pembroke of Port Marlow  <sub>[v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053), [v1 c19 P56](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0056)</sub>

## Quotes

> I solemnly swear to remain loyal to my bosom friend, Isolde Pembroke, for as long as the sun and moon endure.  <sub>[v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035)</sub>

> Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you.  <sub>[v1 c12 P37](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0037)</sub>

> Most certainly I shall, and no other intimate friend will ever be mine—it is not my desire to possess one. Loving anyone else as deeply as I love you is impossible for me.  <sub>[v1 c17 P5](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0005)</sub>

> You can be certain that my love for you, Nell, is devoted and will last forever  <sub>[v1 c17 P9](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0009)</sub>
